claim: Ostreococcus tauri is a ubiquitous picophytoplankton in the ocean.
source: As a ubiquitous picophytoplankton in the ocean and an early-branching green alga, Ostreococcus tauri is a model prasinophyte species for studying the functional evolution of the light-harvesting systems in photosynthesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of O. tauri.

claim: Ostreococcus tauri is an early-branching green alga.
source: As a ubiquitous picophytoplankton in the ocean and an early-branching green alga, Ostreococcus tauri is a model prasinophyte species for studying the functional evolution of the light-harvesting systems in photosynthesis.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of O. tauri.

claim: The O. tauri PSI supercomplex expands its photon-absorbing capacity in low light conditions by assembling with LHCI and Lhcp.
source: Here, we report the structure and function of the O. tauri photosystem I (PSI) supercomplex in low light conditions, where it expands its photon-absorbing capacity by assembling with the light-harvesting complexes I (LHCI) and a prasinophyte-specific light-harvesting complex (Lhcp).
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding of the study.

claim: The architecture of the O. tauri PSI supercomplex exhibits hybrid features of plant-type and green algal-type PSI supercomplexes.
source: The architecture of the supercomplex exhibits hybrid features of the plant-type and the green algal-type PSI supercomplexes, consisting of a PSI core, an Lhca1-Lhca4-Lhca2-Lhca3 belt attached on one side and an Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer associated on the other side between PsaG and PsaH.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a structural finding.

claim: The O. tauri PSI supercomplex consists of a PSI core, an Lhca1-Lhca4-Lhca2-Lhca3 belt attached on one side and an Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer associated on the other side between PsaG and PsaH.

evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a structural finding.

claim: Nine Lhcp subunits, including one Lhcp1 monomer with a phosphorylated amino-terminal threonine and eight Lhcp2 monomers, oligomerize into three trimers and associate with PSI on the third side between Lhca6 and PsaK.
source: Interestingly, nine Lhcp subunits, including one Lhcp1 monomer with a phosphorylated amino-terminal threonine and eight Lhcp2 monomers, oligomerize into three trimers and associate with PSI on the third side between Lhca6 and PsaK.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a structural finding.

claim: The Lhcp1 phosphorylation and the light-harvesting capacity of PSI were subjected to reversible photoacclimation.
source: The Lhcp1 phosphorylation and the light-harvesting capacity of PSI were subjected to reversible photoacclimation, suggesting that the formation of OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is likely due to a phosphorylation-dependent mechanism induced by changes in light intensity.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an experimental finding.

claim: The formation of OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is likely due to a phosphorylation-dependent mechanism induced by changes in light intensity.

claim: The OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex did not exhibit far-red peaks in the 77 K fluorescence spectra.
source: Notably, this supercomplex did not exhibit far-red peaks in the 77 K fluorescence spectra, which is possibly due to the weak coupling of the chlorophyll a603-a609 pair in OtLhca1-4.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an experimental observation.

claim: The absence of far-red peaks in the 77 K fluorescence spectra is possibly due to the weak coupling of the chlorophyll a603-a609 pair in OtLhca1-4.

claim: Ostreococcus tauri is the smallest free-living eukaryote.
source: It is also known as the smallest free-living eukaryote (Courties et al., 1994) and belongs to Prasinophyceae, a class of green algae at the near basal position in the evolution of green lineage and most closely related to the first green alga known as 'ancestral green flagellate' (Lewis and McCourt, 2004).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Courties et al., 1994.

claim: Ostreococcus tauri belongs to Prasinophyceae, a class of green algae at the near basal position in the evolution of green lineage.

claim: A prasinophyte-specific Lhc protein named Lhcp was found in O. tauri.
source: A prasinophyte-specific Lhc protein named Lhcp was found in O. tauri (Six et al., 2005; Swingley et al., 2010) and Mantoniella squamata (another member of Prasinophyceae) (Jiao and Fawley, 1994; Schmitt et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with citations to Six et al., 2005 and Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: Lhcp was found in Mantoniella squamata.
source: A prasinophyte-specific Lhc protein named Lhcp was found in O. tauri (Six et al., 2005; Swingley et al., 2010) and Mantoniella squamata (another member of Prasinophyceae) (Jiao and Fawley, 1994; Schmitt et al., 1994).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with citations to Jiao and Fawley, 1994 and Schmitt et al., 1994.

claim: There are two classes of Lhcp (Lhcp1 and Lhcp2) in O. tauri.
source: There are two classes of Lhcp (Lhcp1 and Lhcp2) in addition to the common LHC proteins, namely six Lhca proteins (Lhca1-6) and two minor monomeric Lhcb proteins (Lhcb4 and Lhcb5), serving as the peripheral antennae of O. tauri PSI and PSII (Six et al., 2005; Swingley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with citations to Six et al., 2005 and Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: O. tauri has six Lhca proteins (Lhca1-6) and two minor monomeric Lhcb proteins (Lhcb4 and Lhcb5).
source: There are two classes of Lhcp (Lhcp1 and Lhcp2) in addition to the common LHC proteins, namely six Lhca proteins (Lhca1-6) and two minor monomeric Lhcb proteins (Lhcb4 and Lhcb5), serving as the peripheral antennae of O. tauri PSI and PSII (Six et al., 2005; Swingley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with citations to Six et al., 2005 and Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: Lhcp proteins form a highly abundant antenna complexes in O. tauri.
source: The Lhcp proteins form a highly abundant antenna complexes in O. tauri (Swingley et al., 2010), and the carotenoid composition of the OtLhcp complexes is largely different from those of LHCIs or light-harvesting complexes II (LHCIIs) in plants and other green algae (such as a core chlorophyte Chlamydomonas reinhardtii) (Minagawa, 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: The carotenoid composition of the OtLhcp complexes is largely different from those of LHCIs or LHCIIs in plants and other green algae.
source: The Lhcp proteins form a highly abundant antenna complexes in O. tauri (Swingley et al., 2010), and the carotenoid composition of the OtLhcp complexes is largely different from those of LHCIs or light-harvesting complexes II (LHCIIs) in plants and other green algae (such as a core chlorophyte Chlamydomonas reinhardtii) (Minagawa, 2009).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Minagawa, 2009.

claim: Lhcp proteins form a separate clade with characteristics of an ancestral state of LHC proteins instead of belonging to the clades of Lhcb or Lhca.
source: While Lhcp, Lhcb (apoproteins of LHCII), and Lhca (apoproteins of LHCI) all belong to the LHC superfamily, Lhcp proteins form a separate clade with characteristics of an ancestral state of LHC proteins instead of belonging to the clades of Lhcb or Lhca (Six et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Six et al., 2005.

claim: The organization of pigment molecules within the Lhcp complexes exhibits distinct features in comparison with plant LHCII.
source: Moreover, the organization of pigment molecules within the Lhcp complexes exhibits distinct features in comparison with plant LHCII according to a previous spectroscopic study (Goss et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Goss et al., 2000.

claim: Under low light conditions, the Lhcp complexes of O. tauri can assemble with the PSI-LHCI to form a larger PSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex.
source: Under low light (LL) conditions, the Lhcp complexes of O. tauri can assemble with the PSI-LHCI to form a larger PSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex, whereas the amount of PSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is greatly reduced under high-light (HL) conditions (Swingley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: The amount of PSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is greatly reduced under high-light conditions.
source: Under low light (LL) conditions, the Lhcp complexes of O. tauri can assemble with the PSI-LHCI to form a larger PSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex, whereas the amount of PSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is greatly reduced under high-light (HL) conditions (Swingley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction with a citation to Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: The most abundant light-harvesting carotenoid in the A3L fraction is prasinoxanthin.
source: Pigment composition analysis of the A3L fraction demonstrates that the most abundant light-harvesting carotenoid is prasinoxanthin (Prx, which is unique to prasinophytes), among other carotenoids of lesser abundance, including dihydrolutein (Dlt) and micromonal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c and Table 1.

claim: Prasinoxanthin is unique to prasinophytes.
source: Pigment composition analysis of the A3L fraction demonstrates that the most abundant light-harvesting carotenoid is prasinoxanthin (Prx, which is unique to prasinophytes), among other carotenoids of lesser abundance, including dihydrolutein (Dlt) and micromonal (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: Lutein was not detected in O. tauri.
source: Although the typical Chls (such as Chl a and Chl b) and carotenoids (violaxanthin/Vio, 9'-cis-neoxanthin/Nex and β-carotene) found in green plants were also present in O. tauri, lutein (a major carotenoid found in plant LHCII) was not detected.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section.

claim: A3 is primarily composed of polypeptides for PSI-LHCI supercomplex.
source: These findings indicate that A3 is primarily composed of polypeptides for PSI-LHCI supercomplex, whereas A3L includes Lhcp1 and Lhcp2 alongside the constituents present in A3, along with comigrated PSII polypeptides, which is essentially in agreement with a previous report (Swingley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a citation to Swingley et al., 2010.

claim: A3L includes Lhcp1 and Lhcp2 alongside the constituents present in A3, along with comigrated PSII polypeptides.
source: These findings indicate that A3 is primarily composed of polypeptides for PSI-LHCI supercomplex, whereas A3L includes Lhcp1 and Lhcp2 alongside the constituents present in A3, along with comigrated PSII polypeptides, which is essentially in agreement with a previous report (Swingley et al., 2010).

claim: The PSI antenna size in A3L was larger than that of A3.

claim: The 77 K fluorescence spectra of PSI-LHCI and PSI-LHCI-Lhcp exhibit a peak at 690 and 680 nm, respectively.

claim: There are no distinctive far-red peaks in the 77 K fluorescence spectra of PSI-LHCI and PSI-LHCI-Lhcp.
source: Notably, the 77 K fluorescence spectra of PSI-LHCI and PSI-LHCI-Lhcp exhibit a peak at 690 and 680 nm, respectively (Figure 1b), and there are no distinctive far-red peaks as reported previously (Swingley et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a citation to Swingley et al., 2010 and supported by data in Figure 1b.

claim: A3 almost exclusively consists of PSI-LHCI supercomplex.

claim: The structure of OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is solved at an overall resolution of 2.94 Å.
source: Through the single-particle cryo-EM method, the structure of OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is solved at an overall resolution of 2.94 Å and the local regions of three Lhcp trimers (namely Trimers 1–3) are refined to 2.9–3.5 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Table 3).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Table 3.

claim: The local regions of three Lhcp trimers are refined to 2.9–3.5 Å.
source: Through the single-particle cryo-EM method, the structure of OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex is solved at an overall resolution of 2.94 Å and the local regions of three Lhcp trimers (namely Trimers 1–3) are refined to 2.9–3.5 Å (Figure 2—figure supplement 1, Table 3).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and Table 3.

claim: The OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex consists of a central PSI monomer encircled by six LHCIs and three Trimers.
source: As shown in Figure 2, the OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex consists of a central PSI monomer encircled by six LHCIs and three Trimers.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: OtPSI contains two large core subunits (PsaA and PsaB), three subunits on the stromal surface (PsaC, PsaD, and PsaE), nine small membrane-embedded subunits (PsaF, PsaG, PsaH, PsaI, PsaJ, PsaK, PsaL, PsaM, PsaO), and one subunit on the lumenal surface (PsaN).
source: OtPSI contains two large core subunits (PsaA and PsaB), three subunits on the stromal surface (PsaC, PsaD, and PsaE) (Figure 2a–c), nine small membrane-embedded subunits (PsaF, PsaG, PsaH, PsaI, PsaJ, PsaK, PsaL, PsaM, PsaO), one subunit on the lumenal surface (PsaN) (Figure 2d–f).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: In the supercomplex, a total of 314 Chls (245 Chl a, 60 Chl b, 9 Mdp), 104 carotenoids, 2 phylloquinones, and 3 Fe4S4 clusters have been located.
source: In the supercomplex, a total of 314 Chls (245 Chl a, 60 Chl b, 9 magnesium 2,4-divinylpheoporphyrin a5 monomethyl ester [Mdp], 104 carotenoids, 2 phylloquinones, and 3 Fe4S4 clusters have been located [Table 4]).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Table 4.

claim: The structure of OtPSI has the largest number of subunits among the structures of PSI known so far.
source: To our best knowledge, the structure of OtPSI has the largest number of subunits among the structures of PSI known so far (including those from plants, green algae, diatom, red algae, and cyanobacteria, Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Four Lhca (Lhca1-4) complexes are associated with the PSI core at the side of PsaG-F-J-K, similar to those found in plant PSI-LHCI complexes.
source: Four Lhca (Lhca1-4) complexes are associated with the PSI core at the side of PsaG- F-J-K (Figure 2a and d), similar to those found in plant PSI-LHCI complexes (Mazor et al., 2017; Qin et al., 2015; Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations to Mazor et al., 2017 and Qin et al., 2015, and supported by data in Figure 2 and Figure 3.

claim: An Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer is associated with the PSI core on the other side formed by PsaG-I-M-H.
source: On the other side formed by PsaG-I-M-H, an Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer is associated with the PSI core (Figure 2a and d).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: The location of Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer overlaps with that of Lhca9-Lhca2 heterodimer associated with C. reinhardtii PSI or Lhcr2-Lhcr1 heterodimer associated with Cyanidioschyzon merolae PSI.
source: The location of Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer overlaps with that of Lhca9-Lhca2 heterodimer associated with C. reinhardtii PSI (Su et al., 2019; Suga et al., 2019) or Lhcr2-Lhcr1 heterodimer associated with Cyanidioschyzon merolae PSI (Pi et al., 2018), whereas the corresponding sites are vacant in plant PSI structures (Mazor et al., 2017; Pan et al., 2018; Qin et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations to Su et al., 2019; Suga et al., 2019; Pi et al., 2018; Mazor et al., 2017; Pan et al., 2018; Qin et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2021.

claim: The corresponding sites for Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer are vacant in plant PSI structures.
source: The location of Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer overlaps with that of Lhca9-Lhca2 heterodimer associated with C. reinhardtii PSI (Su et al., 2019; Suga et al., 2019) or Lhcr2-Lhcr1 heterodimer associated with Cyanidioschyzon merolae PSI (Pi et al., 2018), whereas the corresponding sites are vacant in plant PSI structures (Mazor et al., 2017; Pan et al., 2018; Qin et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations to Mazor et al., 2017; Pan et al., 2018; Qin et al., 2015; Yan et al., 2021.

claim: The fourth helix of OtLhca6 and PsaM coexist in O. tauri.
source: While the fourth transmembrane helix of CrLhca2 or Lhca5 from Dunaliella salina (also known as transmembrane helix F/TMF or TMH4), located at the dimerization interface of the Lhca2/Lhca9 or Lhca5-Lhca6 heterodimer, was previously proposed to replace the role of PsaM in mediating assembly of the LHCI heterodimer with PSI (Caspy et al., 2020; Suga et al., 2019), the fourth helix of OtLhca6 and PsaM coexist in O. tauri.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations to Caspy et al., 2020 and Suga et al., 2019.

claim: PsaM is present in moss and cyanobacteria, where LHCI heterodimer is absent at this position.
source: As PsaM is also present in moss (Gorski et al., 2022) and cyanobacteria (Jordan et al., 2001), where LHCI heterodimer is absent at this position, the role and the origin of the fourth helix of the Lhca proteins might not be directly related to PsaM and need to be revisited.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with citations to Gorski et al., 2022 and Jordan et al., 2001.

claim: The role and the origin of the fourth helix of the Lhca proteins might not be directly related to PsaM and need to be revisited.
source: As PsaM is also present in moss (Gorski et al., 2022) and cyanobacteria (Jordan et al., 2001), where LHCI heterodimer is absent at this position, the role and the origin of the fourth helix of the Lhca proteins might not be directly related to PsaM and need to be revisited.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as a conclusion based on the structural findings.

claim: Plant and C. reinhardtii PSI complexes contain some red-form Chls, absorbing photons at energy levels below that of the primary donor and mainly located in the LHCI complexes.
source: Previously, it was found that plant and C. reinhardtii PSI complexes contain some red-form Chls, absorbing photons at energy levels below that of the primary donor and mainly located in the LHCI complexes (Croce and van Amerongen, 2013).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a citation to Croce and van Amerongen, 2013.

claim: OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex sample does not exhibit far-red peaks in the 77 K fluorescence spectra.
source: Unlike plant and C. reinhardtii PSI, OtPSI-LHCI-Lhcp supercomplex sample does not exhibit far-red peaks in the 77 K fluorescence spectra (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 1b.

claim: In the OtPSI-LHCI, the Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca1-4 are separated at larger distances.
source: In the OtPSI-LHCI, the Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca1-4 (corresponding to the red-form Chls found in plant and C. reinhardtii Lhca1-4) are separated at larger distances, while those in Lhca5 and Lhca6 are similar to the ones in Lhca9 and Lhca2 from C. reinhardtii (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The Chl a603-a609 pairs in Lhca5 and Lhca6 are similar to the ones in Lhca9 and Lhca2 from C. reinhardtii.
source: In the OtPSI-LHCI, the Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca1-4 (corresponding to the red-form Chls found in plant and C. reinhardtii Lhca1-4) are separated at larger distances, while those in Lhca5 and Lhca6 are similar to the ones in Lhca9 and Lhca2 from C. reinhardtii (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4.

claim: The axial ligands of Chl a603 in Lhca1-4 from O. tauri are all His residues instead of Asn.
source: Moreover, the axial ligands of Chl a603 in Lhca1-4 from O. tauri are all His residues instead of Asn (Figure 4b–e).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4b–e.

claim: Mutation of Asn to His for the ligand of Chl a603 in plant Lhca3 and Lhca4 led to absence of red spectral forms.
source: Mutation of Asn to His for the ligand of Chl a603 in plant Lhca3 and Lhca4 led to absence of red spectral forms, while substitution of Asn for His in Lhca1 caused red shift of the fluorescence emission (Morosinotto et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a citation to Morosinotto et al., 2003.

claim: Substitution of Asn for His in Lhca1 caused red shift of the fluorescence emission.
source: Mutation of Asn to His for the ligand of Chl a603 in plant Lhca3 and Lhca4 led to absence of red spectral forms, while substitution of Asn for His in Lhca1 caused red shift of the fluorescence emission (Morosinotto et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a citation to Morosinotto et al., 2003.

claim: The position of Chl a603 in OtLhca1-4 is located farther away from the protein backbone in comparison with those from plant and C. reinhardtii LHCIs.
source: As His has longer side chain than Asn, the position of Chl a603 in OtLhca1-4 is located farther away from the protein backbone (in comparison with those from plant and C. reinhardtii LHCIs) so that the distance between Chl a603 and Chl a609 becomes larger and their excitonic coupling strength might be reduced as a result.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as an inference based on the structural findings.

claim: The distance between Chl a603 and Chl a609 becomes larger and their excitonic coupling strength might be reduced as a result.
source: As His has longer side chain than Asn, the position of Chl a603 in OtLhca1-4 is located farther away from the protein backbone (in comparison with those from plant and C. reinhardtii LHCIs) so that the distance between Chl a603 and Chl a609 becomes larger and their excitonic coupling strength might be reduced as a result.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section as a speculation based on the structural findings.

claim: The axial ligands of Chl a603 in Lhca5-Lhca6 dimer from O. tauri are both Asn residues same as those in the Lhca9-Lhca2 dimer on a similar location in C. reinhardtii.
source: The axial ligands of Chl a603 in Lhca5-Lhca6 dimer from O. tauri are both Asn residues same as those in the Lhca9-Lhca2 dimer on a similar location in C. reinhardtii (Figure 4b–e).
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4b–e.

claim: Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca9 and Lhca2 were proposed to be responsible for the red spectral forms in C. reinhardtii.
source: Although Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca9 and Lhca2 were proposed to be responsible for the red spectral forms in C. reinhardtii (Mozzo et al., 2010), those in OtLhca5 and OtLhca6 with similar configuration do not cause the red spectral forms (Figure 4f and g), indicating that the presence of Asn residues at the axial ligand site is not sufficient to cause the spectral red form of Chl a603/a609.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section with a citation to Mozzo et al., 2010.

claim: Chl a603-a609 pairs in OtLhca5 and OtLhca6 with similar configuration do not cause the red spectral forms.
source: Although Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca9 and Lhca2 were proposed to be responsible for the red spectral forms in C. reinhardtii (Mozzo et al., 2010), those in OtLhca5 and OtLhca6 with similar configuration do not cause the red spectral forms (Figure 4f and g), indicating that the presence of Asn residues at the axial ligand site is not sufficient to cause the spectral red form of Chl a603/a609.
evidence: This is stated directly in the results section and supported by data in Figure 4f and g.

claim: The presence of Asn residues at the axial ligand site is not sufficient to cause the spectral red form of Chl a603/a609.
source: Although Chl a603-a609 pairs of Lhca9 and Lhca2 were proposed to be responsible for the red spectral forms in C. reinhardtii (Mozzo et al., 2010), those in OtLhca5 and OtLhca6 with similar configuration do not cause the red spectral forms (Figure 4f and g), indicating that the presence of Asn residues at the axial ligand site is not sufficient to cause the spectral red form of Chl a603/a609.
